text:
alex_infra: Heads up — NA-west GPU pool (gpu-pool-na-west-9) is showing sustained memory pressure and an uptick in 5xxs. 96% GPU mem, inflight requests 2.3x baseline, 503 rate ~18% over last 3m. Suggest soft-drain new sessions from NA to EU for a short window while we scale and evict stubborn pods. No full failover unless folks object.

maria_sre: Can you paste the queries causing the pressure? Is this model NVMe spill or KV-cache growth? Also worried about p95 for chat — EU p95 is usually 140ms, NA p95 is 80ms. That could impact UX.

alex_infra: Quick look — long-running rerank jobs + several large-batch eval runs accidentally hit the pool. KV cache size per-session spiked (many long contexts). Not NVMe yet. We should avoid moving existing connections, only steer new sessions. Proposed command to change routing weights (will keep a 60s drain window):
```
curl -X POST https://glb.internal.redwood/api/v1/policies/edge-weight-update \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"policy":"prod-edge","overrides":{"na-west":0.35,"eu-west":0.65},"drain_seconds":60}'
```

devon_platform: +1 to soft-drain. Also suggest we enable spillover to dedicated fallback for long sessions so EU doesn't get overloaded with large contexts. Example snippet to attach spillover set for >10s sessions: 
```yaml
routing: 
  policy: prod-edge
  overrides:
    na-west: 0.35
    eu-west: 0.65
  spillover:
    threshold_seconds: 10
    target: dedicated-fallback-na
```
I can apply via infra console if we agree.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaling_up triggered for eu-west-gpu-pool (requested 4 -> provisioning 2 extra nodes).

tyler_oncall: I'm going to apply the GLB weight change via console now with drain 60s. Will watch error rates and p95. Ping me if we need faster change.

ops-bot: alert: gpu-pool-eu-west utilization at 79% (threshold 80%).

tyler_oncall: Applied weights 0.35/0.65, drain=60s. After 90s error rate in NA-west down to 6%, overall 5xxs decreased. EU p95 rose to ~210ms for a subset of requests. EU GPU usage jumped to 84% — we should be careful not to tip it.

julia_prod: Heads up — cross-region traffic is increasing token egress costs because of larger response sizes. If EU stays the heavier carrier for long, costs will spike. Can we limit cross-region for heavy-generation routes (max tokens > 512)?

alex_infra: Good call — let's update routing to prefer local region for requests where token limit >512 and only spill to EU for sessions <512 tokens. Also enable prefix-cache replication for popular prefixes to warm EU. Command to trigger cache replication (one-off):
```
POST /cache/replicate HTTP/1.1
Host: cachemgr.internal.redwood
Authorization: Bearer $CACHE_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{"prefixes":["/user/typing/","/evals/common/"],"target":"eu-west"}
```

maria_sre: Agree to token-based routing. That should reduce large-gen cross-region. Also set a hard cap so spillover doesn't target EU more than 65% to avoid saturation.

devon_platform: I'll push the routing tweak (prefer-local for >512) and enable spillover to dedicated-fallback-na for long sessions. Yanking the config now.

ops-bot: autoscaler: eu-west-gpu-pool provisioning complete (+2 nodes). Monitoring for 10m.

tyler_oncall: Results after changes: NA 5xxs back to baseline, EU p95 tapered to 160ms after cache replication warmup, eu-west GPU usage stabilized at 78%. Cost meter shows a small egress uptick but within expected emergency limits.

julia_prod: OK — monitor cost and set a watch if 24h avg delta > 12%.

alex_infra: Decision: 1) soft-drain new sessions to eu-west with weights na-west:0.4 eu-west:0.6, drain_seconds=45, 2) enable spillover to dedicated-fallback-na for sessions longer than 10s or token_limit>1024, 3) replicate hot prefixes to eu-west. We'll keep this config for 15 minutes and reassess. Agree? :thumbsup:

maria_sre: 👍 monitoring dashboards and will alert if EU crosses 85% or NA errors rise.

devon_platform: Done — configs pushed and stored under infra/configs/routing/1845009876-emergency.json.

tyler_oncall: Leaving increased retention on relevant traces for 1h to help postmortem. I'll close this thread if things stay stable for 15m.

ops-bot: note: incident-marker created: incident/1845009876-edge-traffic-drain.

alex_infra: Thanks team — follow-up after 15m with TL;DR and any further action items.
